Middle East.headline: Yemen, Saudi Arabia launch new strikes against Houthis in bid to retake lost territory
Middle East.body: The Yemeni military, backed by Saudi jets, began a broad set of strikes on Monday against Iran-backed Houthi targets in an attempt to retake lost territory. The Houthis launched an offensive in September, which killed hundreds of combatants on both sides, according to UN figures, and has since become the most active front in the wider Middle East war.

Middle East.body: Escalating conflict in Yemen has resulted in 5,166 casualties, including 959 deaths, since early August 2026, the World Health Organization announced on Monday. A new situation report details a crisis rapidly expanding toward the country's eastern governorates. Renewed violence is driving mass displacement and compounding severe public health vulnerabilities, most notably a cholera resurgence among populations fleeing active front lines. The WHO's sixth situation report, which covers the six-day period from September 27 to October 2, documented 685 new casualties, comprising 121 fatalities and 564 injuries. Americas.headline: Canada Extends Ebola Immigration Measures to Nov. 27
Americas.body: Advertisement Canada has renewed its Ebola-related immigration restrictions for another 60 days, keeping travel documents suspended for residents of three central African countries through November 27, 2026. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada announced the extension on September 28, 2026, saying it remains "deeply concerned about the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the evolving risk of Ebola disease in neighbouring countries, including Uganda and South Sudan." Americas.headline: New Data Reveals Nearly 1.5 Million Displaced In Haiti As Instability Escalates
Americas.body: As armed gangs continue to act as de facto authorities in Haiti, recent reports reveal that approximately 12 percent of the population, roughly 1.5 million Haitians, are now displaced, according to data collected by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Additionally, 80 percent of people being displaced are located outside of Port-au-Prince, Haiti’s capital and largest city, with the most significant increase recorded in Haiti’s Artibonite department, a rural northern region, where displacement rose by 16 percent between May and August 2026, according to the IOM. Africa.headline: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Records More than 4,000 Deaths as Authorities Struggle to Contai...
Africa.body: Congo's Ebola outbreak has now recorded more than 4,000 deaths, authorities said as they struggle to contain the spread of the virus. The latest figures were released by the health ministry on Thursday. They show that 4,018 people have died from among 8,300 confirmed cases, making up for nearly half of the confirmed cases in what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Congo announced an outbreak on May 15, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no known treatment or vaccine, The Associated Press said. The World Health Organization has recently raised the alarm regarding the rapid geographical spread of the virus into new health zones, stretching limited resources.

Africa.headline: Inside the study for a remedy to fight Congo’s deadliest Ebola outbreak
Africa.body: More than 250 participants have been enrolled in a trial for a drug that could stop them from contracting Ebola in Congo, in what experts have described as a critical step to try to fight the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the Central African country. The drug is targeted at Bundibugyo virus, which is responsible for the fast-moving outbreak and is without an approved vaccine or treatment. The trial began in July and is one of several studies launched to find some protection and another way of at least slowing the outbreak.

Africa.headline: Congo’s Ebola outbreak has killed more than 4,000, government data shows
Africa.body: Audio By Carbonatix The number of deaths in Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 4,000, government data showed on Friday, as the worst epidemic in the country's history resists containment efforts. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, became the largest and deadliest in Congo after surpassing the 2018-2020 epidemic. It is now second only to the 2014-2016 West African Ebola outbreak, which infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000 across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. Asia-Pacific.headline: Nepal Flood Tragedy: 157 killed, 500 including 100 Indians and foreign tourists missing
Asia-Pacific.body: AMN / NEWS DESK A devastating flash flood triggered by an avalanche in Nepal’s northern Himalayas killed at least 157 people and left hundreds missing on Wednesday, sweeping through communities, destroying infrastructure and washing away vehicles, homes and major public facilities across three districts. The disaster struck without warning along the Bhotekoshi River, near Nepal’s border with China, after an avalanche is believed to have blocked the flow of the Lhende tributary and created a sudden surge of water and debris. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: MSF: North Kivu's Ebola outbreak spreading like a megafire as new hotspots multiply
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: MSF: North Kivu's Ebola outbreak spreading like a megafire as new hotspots multiply 05 Oct 2026 - The Ebola outbreak in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, has intensified dramatically since early September, with the province now accounting for nearly 40% of all newly confirmed cases nationwide, up from 24% at the end of August. With new hotspots emerging every week, treatment capacities remain largely insufficient and inadequate. This situation places both current patients and entire communities at even greater risk. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: France steps up international support to combat Ebola and strengthen epidemic response
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Paris, France – The French Foreign Minister affirmed his country’s commitment to continuing and strengthening efforts to support international initiatives aimed at eradicating the Ebola epidemic. He also emphasized the importance of intensifying cooperation among nations and international organizations to combat the spread of infectious diseases. The Minister explained that fighting Ebola goes beyond merely treating infected cases; it requires a comprehensive system encompassing prevention, rapid detection, contact tracing, and the provision of necessary medical care.
